trainers.instruction: This is a map of West Africa. Select the city to learn more.

atoms.b: Lagos is a port city in Nigeria. It is the largest city in ((++West East)) Africa, with a population of 22 million people. As the home of many banks and technology companies, Lagos is continuing to experience very ((++fast slow)) growth.

Lagos is built behind a series of barrier islands, which are long, narrow strips of land that run parallel to the coastline. These islands create lagoons that are protected from the ((++strong weak)) Atlantic currents.
The city’s ports make use of this unique geography. The ships have easy access to the Atlantic Ocean but are also ((++protected threatened)) from the open water at the same time.

trainers.instruction: Select the cocoa bean to learn more.

instruction.text: Many goods are produced in the Ivory Coast. Match each product to the correct image.

feedback.finish: Ivory Coast is the largest producer of cocoa beans in the world, making up around 40% of the global market. Their gold industry has also been growing since the discovery of a large deposit in 2024.

atoms.b: Lake Retba in Senegal is famous for its ((++pink yellow)) water, which is caused by a type of algae that can be found there.
The lake is not just a popular tourist destination because of its colour. Its high salt concentration also allows visitors to ((++float sink)) effortlessly, making it a unique swimming experience.

Extracting this salt from Lake Retba is also ((++important insignificant)) for the region’s economy. Workers use long poles to loosen the salt before harvesting. Once collected, it is exported across the region.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: West Africa is home to hundreds of different languages and peoples, each with their own separate identity. However, the region’s shared history of ancient kingdoms, colonisation and trade means many countries also share similar food, music and traditions.

West Africa’s most famous dish is jollof rice. Jollof originates from Senegal but is also common in other countries, such as Nigeria and Ghana. Each country has its own variation, which creates friendly competition across the region.

Countries such as Mali, Guinea and Burkina Faso are known for the djembe: a drum made from a single piece of wood and a goatskin cover. The djembe is traditionally played at ceremonies like weddings, baptisms and harvests.
